report_name: Wesco Investigates CRM Breach After ExfilSquad Claims Data Theft

threat_actors.name: ExfilSquad
threat_actors.description: A data extortion group that claimed responsibility for the Wesco breach. The group is known for stealing data from misconfigured cloud applications, particularly Microsoft Power Pages, and leaking it on their dark web site if a ransom is not paid. They do not typically deploy ransomware.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through the theft and threatened release of sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: ExfilSquad likely scanned for public-facing Microsoft Power Pages portals with misconfigured table permissions that allow anonymous users to access data.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The attack vector was a suspected security misconfiguration in Wesco's cloud CRM platform (Microsoft Power Pages or Dynamics 365), which allowed anonymous users to access sensitive data tables.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Upon discovering the vulnerable portal, ExfilSquad used APIs to systematically query and exfiltrate 2.6 million records from the exposed Microsoft Dataverse tables.

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: ExfilSquad used the 2.6 million stolen records for financial extortion, demanding a ransom from Wesco and leaking the data when the demand was not met.

identities.name: Wesco
identities.description: A Fortune 500 global supply chain and distribution company that suffered a data breach of its cloud CRM environment. The breach resulted in the theft and public leak of 2.6 million customer and employee records.

infrastructure.name: ExfilSquad Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site controlled by ExfilSquad used to publish the 2.6 million records stolen from Wesco after the ransom demand was not met.

indicators.name: Anomalous Data Access from Microsoft Power Pages
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Read Access from Anonymous Power Pages User
id: 2b1c8e4a-9f0d-4c5a-8b3d-1e7f6a9b0c2d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects when an anonymous or unauthenticated user performs a high volume of read operations in a Power Platform environment. This could indicate data scraping from a misconfigured Power Pages portal, as seen in the Wesco breach by ExfilSquad.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wesco-confirms-security-incident-after-exfilsquad-claims-data-theft/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-13
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.collection
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: powerplatform
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate public-facing portals may generate these events. Correlation is required to identify unusually high volumes from a single source IP or user.
level: medium
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'RetrieveMultiple'
    UserId|contains: 
      - '#Portals'
      - 'POWERPAGES_ANONYMOUS'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of read operations from an unauthenticated user or a single IP address against a Microsoft Power Pages/Dataverse environment, which could indicate data scraping from a misconfigured portal.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Data Access from Microsoft Power Pages
